A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SYMPOL despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V2 reports original PPO and A2C benchmark results, component ablations, runtime measurements, and a DistShift misgeneralization case study.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds evaluated VIPER comparisons and illustrative learned-tree analyses.

M1.justification: The GradTree actor, separate neural critic, straight-through optimization, selective weight decay, dynamic rollout and batch sizes, and continuous-action formulation are retained. The learning-rate reduction description moves from Section 4.1 to Appendix C; it is not removed from the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five control environments, five MiniGrid settings, and randomized DistShift scenarios. The added VIPER comparisons and tree illustrations use existing task coverage.

E2.justification: VIPER, previously discussed but not evaluated, becomes a direct comparator at depths 5 and 8 in v3 Tables 8–9. Its inclusion across CartPole, Acrobot, LunarLander, and all five MiniGrid settings substantially expands comparison with established tree-policy methods. Existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: New Appendix A.5 uses smaller SDTs for illustration, explicitly reporting size 4 versus size 7 in evaluation. This introduces a limited configuration difference for the new analysis. The existing million-timestep training budget, 60-trial hyperparameter search, and benchmark evaluation procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 Appendix A.5 adds a qualitative interpretability comparison using a 59-node CartPole tree and soft-tree examples for CartPole and MountainCar. It examines larger-tree readability and probabilistic routing. Existing component ablations, A2C analyses, and DistShift case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random trainings with five evaluation episodes each, Cohen’s D, and significance-based table bolding. V3 introduces no specified statistical-estimation procedure or increased-run count; its new comparison tables follow the existing reporting convention.

E6.justification: V3 Tables 8–9 add substantive VIPER results across the existing discrete benchmarks. Depth-8 VIPER scores 480 on CartPole, -169 on LunarLander, 0.801 on LG-7, and 0.954 on DistShift; corresponding unchanged SYMPOL scores are 500, -57, 0.953, and 0.939. Previously reported benchmark, A2C, information-loss, ablation, and runtime table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The MDP definitions, PPO objective, tree-policy equations, splitting formulation, and rollout schedule are unchanged. The added dense-tree illustration and hard-versus-soft discussion explain existing mathematics rather than introduce new definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The substantive claims remain direct optimization of interpretable axis-aligned policies, avoidance of post-processing information loss, framework compatibility, and strong performance and interpretability. V3 foregrounds information loss and itemizes existing components without materially changing these claims’ scope.

C2.justification: Appendix A.5 adds interpretations of high-level versus lower-level tree decisions, possible benefits of further pruning, and difficulties interpreting probability-weighted SDT leaves. Appendix A.3 also qualifies comparisons with published VIPER results through CartPole-version differences and evaluation variability.

D1.justification: V3 explicitly identifies CartPole-v1 and its 500-step horizon when discussing comparability, and discloses the smaller SDT configuration used for illustrations. Code access, hardware, hyperparameter grids, and selected values are retained. The learning-rate schedule disclosure is relocated rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: V3 adds discussion and citations concerning differentiable logic policies, further soft-tree methods, and misgeneralization. It explicitly relates SA-DT to DAGGER/VIPER and expands the distinction between SYMPOL and differentiable trees. The original three broad related-work streams remain.

P1.justification: V3 changes the title, reformats contributions into three explicit points, reorders related-work streams and results discussion, and clarifies method explanations. These are localized narrative revisions; the main section sequence and substantial portions of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 replaces the architecture overview with a standard-versus-dense tree diagram, removes the rollout-size plot, adds selected training curves, two VIPER tables, and three tree-example figures, and redraws existing curves. This substantially changes the visual presentation. Some redrawn-curve captions retain outdated color descriptions.

improvement.justification: The VIPER evaluations close a specific comparator gap, while the dense-tree diagram and Appendix A.5 make the interpretability argument easier to assess. These provide useful additional support and clarity for the retained method and findings. The gains are limited, with minor caption inconsistencies remaining in the redrawn plots.
